sources.cite: AWS. CloudFormation User Guide: Continue rolling back an update
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED when CloudFormation 'can't roll back all the changes', e.g. a resource 'deleted outside of CloudFormation'; 'A stack in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state can't be updated, but it can be rolled back to a working state (UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE)'; continue-update-rollback with --resources-to-skip for resources that failed during the rollback; skipped resources become inconsistent with the template and must be made consistent 'Before performing another stack update', or 'the stack will become unrecoverable'.

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon VPC User Guide: Subnet CIDR blocks
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: an IPv4 subnet is between /28 and /16; five addresses in each subnet are reserved (network, VPC router, DNS, future use, broadcast). A /28 has 16 addresses, so 11 usable.

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon EC2 API Reference: CreateSubnet
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: 'After you create a subnet, you can't change its CIDR block.' 'AWS reserves both the first four and the last IPv4 address in each subnet's CIDR block.'

sources.cite: AWS. CloudFormation Template Reference: DeletionPolicy attribute
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: without a DeletionPolicy 'CloudFormation deletes your resources'; for AWS::RDS::DBInstance without DBClusterIdentifier 'the default policy is Snapshot'.

sources.cite: AWS. CloudFormation User Guide: Update stacks using change sets
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: change sets 'preview how proposed changes to a stack might impact your running resources'; creating one 'doesn't make changes to your stack'; failures from runtime conditions 'might still occur during execution'.

brief.situation: Monday 10:00. Overnight, the update to shop-prod (us-east-2, Ohio) failed and then its rollback failed too: the stack is in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED. The shop still runs on its 4 web instances. Wednesday's flash sale needs 16.
handover: The update raised the Auto Scaling group from 4 to 16 instances and moved them to a new security group, WebSecurityGroupV2, replacing WebSecurityGroupV1.
The web instances run in two subnets, web-a and web-b, created years ago for a small pilot.
The stack also holds the shop's RDS database. Nobody has written down why the rollback failed.
howItWorks: Learner-paced: nothing moves until you act. Read the failure, recover the stack, fix the cause, then run the week.
The board shows the stack and its subnets; the meters show the capacity ready for the sale and the shop's availability.
Before you run the week you are asked what failed and how you fixed it. The debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Instances the flash sale needs, from last year's sale.

plan.question: Before you run the week: why did the update fail, why did the rollback fail, and how did you fix each without making things worse?

parts.label: Two failures
parts.criteria: Reads the stack events: the update failed because the /28 subnets had too few free addresses (11 usable each, mostly used); the rollback failed because the old security group was deleted outside CloudFormation.
parts.modelAnswer: The update could not launch 12 more instances into two /28 subnets with 11 usable addresses each, mostly taken. The rollback then tried to restore a security group a cleanup script had deleted, which CloudFormation still tracked.

parts.label: Recovery and fix
parts.criteria: Continues the update rollback skipping the deleted resource (not deleting the stack, which holds the database); adds new larger subnets because a subnet's CIDR cannot change; reconciles the skipped resource in the next update, ideally previewed with a change set.
parts.modelAnswer: Continue the rollback skipping WebSecurityGroupV1, which brings the stack back without touching the database. Add two /24 subnets in the template, since existing subnets cannot be resized, and move the group there. Rerun through a change set, which also removes the skipped group from the template so the stack and the real resources agree again.

expertPath.text: Stack events: subnet addresses, then a missing security group. Subnets: two /28s nearly full. CloudTrail: a cleanup script deleted the group.
Continue the rollback, skipping WebSecurityGroupV1. Add two /24 subnets in the template.
Rerun through a change set and review it. The trade-off: a slower, previewed update instead of a quick retry on a stack that just failed twice.

outage.headline: Shop outage
outage.body: Deleting the stack took the shop down for hours, and leaving the /28 subnets in place left the sale without capacity. Recover the stack in place and add room for the instances.

fixed.headline: Recovered and carried the sale
fixed.body: You read both failures, recovered the stack without touching the database, fixed the subnet sizing and reconciled the skipped resource in a reviewed update. That is the expert path.

partly.body: Check whether you read the events first, whether the stack was recovered in place, and whether the subnets were fixed.

scoring.modelReasoning: Two separate problems show in the stack events. The update failed because two /28 subnets have only 11 usable addresses each (AWS reserves 5) and were nearly full. The rollback failed because a security group was deleted outside CloudFormation, which still expected it. A stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED cannot be updated; continue the rollback and skip the resource that cannot be restored, then reconcile it in the next update. Deleting the stack would take down the shop and its database. A subnet's CIDR cannot be changed, so add larger subnets and move the Auto Scaling group to them, and preview the rerun with a change set.
